_comment: Provider registry. Edited from /admin, committed to this public repo like any method change. The web app never executes `command`; only the local Python pipeline does. See lib/providers.ts for the security boundary. Extractor order is priority: the first enabled extractor wins, and an enabled API entry beats every CLI below it. The run record stores which one actually ran.

providers.label: Gemini
providers.note: Adapter works and is tested; the models do not. Measured 2026-08-26: gemini-3.5-flash failed 31% of a full week with 503 UNAVAILABLE (and 5 of 8 sequentially, so it is Google's overload, not our concurrency). gemini-3.6-flash answers reliably but chooses to search on roughly a fifth of calls, which measures what the model remembers rather than what it retrieves. Grounding cannot be forced: google_search_retrieval returns 400 and tool_config ANY times out. The whole 2.5 line is 404 for new keys. Re-enable when a stable, reliably-grounded model exists, and bump method_version in the same change.

providers.label: Claude (API)
providers.note: Primary extractor, and the only one that costs no subscription tokens. Runs as one Batch API job per run: half price, and a Monday chart does not care that a read takes minutes instead of seconds. Listed first, so it wins. Measured against 150 stored answers it agrees with the archive on 89% of first-named brands, which is the task's own noise floor. Declared conflict: it reads answers about its own products.

providers.label: Claude Code (local CLI)
providers.note: Fallback, used only when no API key is set. Reads correctly but carries ~48.5k tokens of harness context per call against this machine's subscription, which is ~98% of the call and roughly 55M tokens a week across a full run. That is why the API entry is listed above it.

providers.label: Codex (local CLI)
providers.note: Last-resort extractor, used when neither the API nor claude is available. ~9k tokens of harness overhead per call; cheaper than claude-cli, but still subscription tokens rather than metered ones.

providers.label: Claude Code (local)
providers.note: Own chart row, not a substitute for the hosted claude engine: this is a coding agent with a different system prompt, and it volunteers that it is made by Anthropic. Enabled, which means the weekly run must happen on this machine: see scripts/weekly-run.cmd.

providers.label: Codex (local)
providers.note: Own chart row, not a substitute for the hosted chatgpt engine. In testing it ranked Claude Code above OpenAI's own Codex. Enabled for the same reason as claude-code.
